# Lab 14.15: Configure Cloud NAT for Private VMs

## What We Are Going to Do
Give private VMs outbound internet access for updates with Cloud NAT, while keeping them unreachable from the internet.

## Steps

1. **Create a private VM.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute networks create nat-vpc --subnet-mode=custom
gcloud compute networks subnets create nat-subnet --network=nat-vpc \
  --region=us-central1 --range=10.80.0.0/24
gcloud compute firewall-rules create nat-iap --network=nat-vpc --allow=tcp:22 \
  --source-ranges=35.235.240.0/20
gcloud compute instances create nat-vm --zone=us-central1-a --machine-type=e2-micro \
  --subnet=nat-subnet --no-address</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Try the internet.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute ssh nat-vm --zone=us-central1-a --tunnel-through-iap \
  --command="curl -s -m 5 https://ifconfig.me || echo NO_INTERNET"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   It prints `NO_INTERNET`.

3. **Reserve a static IP and create Cloud NAT.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute addresses create nat-ip --region=us-central1
gcloud compute routers create nat-router --network=nat-vpc --region=us-central1
gcloud compute routers nats create nat-config \
  --router=nat-router --region=us-central1 \
  --nat-all-subnet-ip-ranges \
  --nat-external-ip-pool=nat-ip \
  --enable-logging --log-filter=ALL</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   A static IP lets partners allow-list your outbound address.

4. **Try again.** The same command now prints the static NAT IP.

5. **Check the NAT logs.** In **Logs Explorer**, filter `resource.type="nat_gateway"`.

6. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute instances delete nat-vm --zone=us-central1-a --quiet
gcloud compute routers delete nat-router --region=us-central1 --quiet
gcloud compute addresses delete nat-ip --region=us-central1 --quiet
gcloud compute firewall-rules delete nat-iap --quiet
gcloud compute networks subnets delete nat-subnet --region=us-central1 --quiet
gcloud compute networks delete nat-vpc --quiet</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Outbound internet | Works through NAT |
| Inbound from internet | Still impossible |
| Source IP | Your reserved static address |
| Logs | Connections and errors logged |
